title: Standards-alignment model + framework-license policy
context: Every lesson plan in this project declares the learning standards it meets. Standards alignment is a first-class, verifiable property — not a vague label — but standards frameworks themselves have their own copyright and license terms that are a common trap: descriptor text may not be freely reproducible. Additionally, alignment must be honest: fabricated or sloppy alignments erode teacher trust and are a fundamental quality defect. The project needs a canonical machine-readable alignment model and an explicit per-framework licensing policy before any plan is authored, so contributors know exactly what to record, how to record it, and what framework text they may or may not reproduce.
objective: Define the machine-readable standards-alignment model and the per-framework licensing policy so all lesson plans use consistent, honest, legally safe alignment records that can be emitted as CASE/LRMI metadata later.
acceptanceCriteria: Defines the machine-readable alignment structure: framework (e.g. CCSS, NGSS), stable code (e.g. CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.5.1), optional short descriptor, alignmentRationale (human-written justification), and descriptorLicenseOk boolean.
States the no-fabrication rule: if a plan cannot be honestly aligned to a cited standard, it ships unaligned and labelled as such — never with a false or speculative alignment.

Covers CCSS (Common Core State Standards) framework license: © NGA Center and CCSSO; public license permits use/reproduction with required attribution notice; specifies which attribution notice is required and the limit on descriptor reproduction.
Covers NGSS framework: Creative Commons license by lead states; trademark-use guidance (no implied endorsement); attribution terms.
Defines the default policy for state/national frameworks: code + link only (no descriptor reproduction) until that framework's license is individually verified; describes the verification step.
Specifies that alignment is emittable as CASE-style (1EdTech Competencies & Academic Standards Exchange) and LRMI alignmentObject metadata, with pinned spec versions recorded in specVersions.
The document is the authoritative reference for the CASE/LRMI emitter task (teacher-lesson-plans-casemeta-011) and all plan-authoring tasks.
Document is committed to the repo; no standards descriptor text is reproduced beyond what the relevant framework license verifiably permits.
resources: CCSS public license and attribution requirements — https://www.corestandards.org/public-license/
NGSS license and trademark guidance — https://www.nextgenscience.org/
output: A committed standards-alignment model and framework-license policy document covering: alignment data structure, no-fabrication rule, CCSS/NGSS/default-framework licensing policies, descriptor-reproduction limits and attribution notices, CASE/LRMI emittability specification, and specVersions recording requirement.
